Nez Perce (Nimiipuu)

Nimiipuu, also called Nez Perce, is a people-level route broader than the Nez Perce Tribe's Idaho government. A Wallowa community organization's history connects descendants from several reservations with renewed gathering in wal'áwa; a separate NPS account introduces treaty-era divisions among bands.

Still unfinished

Two actual public narratives provide a focused starting point on Wallowa reconnection and treaty-era differences. They do not supply a broad Nimiipuu history, specialist language coverage or balanced community-authored documentation across the separate governments.

Assessment recorded October 27, 2026. This is separate from research completion and community review.

  • More Nimiipuu-authored histories, language publications and distinct Colville, Umatilla and Idaho community perspectives remain to be reviewed.
  • The nonprofit's account is organizational self-description; independent program evaluation, original oral recordings and long-term restoration outcomes were not examined.
  • Original treaty scans, oral interpretations, band-specific narratives and the linked 1877 material remain unread. No present treaty-rights or homeland-boundary conclusion is proposed.
  • No Nimiipuu community review or endorsement is recorded. The Spalding photograph depicts a public NPS visitor center, not a tribal government building or all Nimiipuu community life.

03

Returning to wal'áwa across reservation communities

Nez Perce Wallowa Homeland traces its beginnings to Taz Conner, a Nez Perce descendant, and local allies. Its account dates the first Tamkaliks homecoming to 1989 and nonprofit formation to 1996. The organization specifically welcomes Nez Perce descendants from Colville, Umatilla and Nez Perce reservations. This provides a community-organization perspective on reconnection; it does not make those different governments interchangeable.

Read the sources [4] Nez Perce Wallowa Homeland

04

Treaty history involved different bands and choices

NPS's treaty-period account distinguishes the 1855 agreement from the 1863 council held after gold discovery. It describes bands outside the proposed smaller reservation rejecting that agreement while other headmen signed it. This history helps explain why a later reservation or one government cannot stand for every Nimiipuu experience. The original documents and different oral understandings still require separate reading.

Read the sources [5] National Park Service

Community organizationNez Perce Wallowa HomelandSource 4

Our Story / Our History — Nez Perce Wallowa Homeland ↗

A Nez Perce descendant-founded nonprofit's own history of renewed access and cultural gathering in wal'áwa. It follows the 1989 Tamkaliks beginning and 1996 nonprofit establishment, and specifically welcomes descendants from Colville, Umatilla and Nez Perce reservations. Its account supports this organization's history; it is neither a tribal government's statement nor an independently evaluated report of program outcomes. No photographs or embedded media reused.

Inspection: Content reviewed for the stated scope

Scope: Actual main narrative lines 76–98 read, including Taz E. E. Conner's attributed 1994 quotation, origins, 1989 event, 1996 incorporation and cross-reservation welcome. Synthesis selects the historical sequence and named descendant connections. No current acreage or service-availability claim, linked programs, original oral recording, financial record or media inspected.

Review recorded: October 27, 2026

The Treaty Period — Nez Perce National Historical Park ↗

A focused federal public-history account of the 1855 and 1863 councils, gold discovery and disagreement among Nimiipuu bands. Useful for explaining why the later reservation and a people are different scopes. This is a summary, not inspection of the original treaty texts, oral understandings or present law. Its statements about reservation reduction are attributed to NPS rather than converted into a new boundary.

Inspection: Content reviewed for the stated scope

Scope: Complete substantive body lines 21–25 read, plus December 29, 2022 update date at line 30. Interactive map, treaty links, images and Flight of 1877 link not inspected. This is a fresh review record with a new ID; baseline p247-s3 is retained unchanged.

Review recorded: October 27, 2026
